review_reference: Owner request of 2026-11-11 (D-Eminence, relayed by the coordinator in the admin dashboard contract): a super admin only activity dashboard (people, care activity, Migrate and Ask, a daily chart, the latest sign-ups and uploads) for 7, 30 or 90 days, with names shortened ("Ada O."), emails masked ("a***@gmail.com") and Health IDs shortened ("HID-7K…M9") inside the database, and every view audited. Numbered 0123: 0109-0121 are held by open pull requests, 0122 by the collect sign-up fields plan, and the coordinator reserved 0123 for this. Unsigned: reviewed_by is empty until the owner signs.
evidence: Single migration 0123_admin_platform_activity.sql, unsigned until the owner signs (reviewed_by is empty). WHAT IT DOES (additive only; no existing table, column, row, policy or function body changes): (1) the permission platform.dashboard.read, granted to platform_super_admin and to no other role; (2) identity.admin_platform_activity(integer) returns jsonb, SECURITY DEFINER, VOLATILE, search_path pinned, EXECUTE for hid_identity_runtime and hid_schema_test_runtime only: 42501 ADMIN_PERMISSION_DENIED unless the session account holds platform.dashboard.read, 22023 ADMIN_INVALID_DAYS unless 7, 30 or 90, one platform audit row per call (action admin.overview.activity.read, details {"days": n} only), the sealed demo tenant left out of every number and list, names, emails, Health IDs and upload file names shortened in SQL; two immutable shorteners granted to no role; (3) a read window for production's non-BYPASSRLS owner: the table identity.admin_activity_read_windows (RLS enabled, no policy, no grant), the helper identity.admin_activity_read_open() (granted to no role) and one permissive SELECT policy TO the applier role only on each of the eleven FORCE row-level-security tables the read counts (ehr.encounters, clinical_notes, vitals, diagnoses, prescriptions, lab_requests, documents, document_scan_events, staff_chat_messages, ocr.publications, outreach.registration_cases), true only while the function holds a window row for its own backend and transaction (inserted after the permission check, deleted before the audit row). No runtime role is a member of the applier, so no runtime query evaluates these policies. Old services: nothing calls the function until the Identity API image with GET /api/v1/admin/overview/activity is deployed. SUITE: services/ehr-api/test/database/admin-platform-activity.integration.sql, 37 cases, rollback-only: who may call (platform_admin, operations admin, disabled super admin, no subject and a patient refused; the super admin accepted), the days accepted, the audit rows, the read window not forgeable by the runtime and closed after each call, the eleven policies, the counts moved by synthetic fixtures, and the shortened values (no whole name, email, Health ID or file name in the answer). Proved on a throwaway local PostgreSQL 16 twice: 0001-0108 + 0123 applied by a superuser (with all 82 database suites passing), and 0001-0108 + 0123 applied by a non-superuser, non-BYPASSRLS migrator with MIGRATION_TARGET=rds (the suite passes; with three of the policies dropped it fails 5d and 6e, so the window is what lets the production owner count).
